newsitem.title: UK: Latam origins prevail among sugar freight enquiry.
newsitem.headline: Latam origins prevail among sugar freight enquiry.

text.p: London's sugar freight market saw a sprinkling of fresh enquiry at the start of the week with Latin American producing nations prevailing amongst the quoted origins, shipbrokers said on Monday.
Genoc quoted two orders from different origins and was still open with its order for 25/30,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Cuba to Egypt.

It was in the market for 14,000 tonnes in bags from Rouen/Antwerp to Iran for end-April and again from Puerto Quetzal to Sri Lanka with Karachi and east Africa options including Madagascar for prompt/14 days notice.
ESTC was open on account for 26,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Cuba to Egypt/Black Sea for May 1/10 with possibility of using timecharter instead.
D.K. Shipping floated an account order for 13,000 tonnes of sugar in 50 kg bags from east coast Mexico to Algeria, Dubai or Yemen for April 20/25.
Seabon's order for 14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from the EU excluding UK to Iran for prompt/10 days was still unfilled, shipbrokers said.
Last week's inquiries from Czarnikow Rionda and Cargill were also open, they added.
